As Ouyang Kan watched Ling Ran’s maneuvers, he recalled his journey of learning how to perform laparoscopy.
He was more than affected by it.
There was practically a storm brewing inside his heart.

Laparoscopy was extremely popular nowadays, and a person would have to go against his conscience to say that Ouyang Kan and the other doctors did not spend time and energy on learning how to use a laparoscope.
In reality, to keep up with the times, Ouyang Kan had spent almost a thousand hours practicing laparoscopy.
However, it took a lot for an untalented doctor to learn something.

If Ouyang Kan were still young and familiarizing himself with this surgical method for the first time, he might be able to spend a few hundred hours to learn laparoscopy, just like how he did with open surgery.
He could then spend a few hundred hours studying laparoscopy and a few hundred more hours improving himself to build a competitive advantage.
However, Ouyang Kan was no longer young.
If he wanted to replace open surgery with laparoscopy, he would at least need to be almost as good at laparoscopy as he was at open surgery.
And truth be told, he no longer had what it took to learn a new surgical method.
He was not a genius and was unable to quickly learn how to perform laparoscopy.
He was also responsible for his own treatment group and had to spend time on that.
Moreover, he did not have a teacher who could guide him in performing laparoscopy.
Hence, laparoscopy was basically beyond his reach.
The hospital and even his department would not put any consideration into ways in which a fifty-year-old surgeon could learn a new surgical method.
All they wanted was for Ouyang Kan to shine brightly during his last moments in the hospital by being one of the last batches of doctors who performed open surgery.
Only genii who were extraordinarily talented could change directions as they pleased so that they could fully realize their worth in this world.
“No signs of metastases in the abdominal aorta and mesentery.” Ling Ran’s voice was loud and clear, and it immediately snapped Ouyang Kan out of his reverie.
Ouyang Kan nodded as he looked at the screen to show his approval.
“The surface of the intestine is clear.
“There’s no metastases in the pancreas and the transverse mesentery.
“There are no metastases in the retroperitoneal lymph nodes.”
Ling Ran was not in a hurry to remove the tumor from the stomach.
Instead, he looked around the primary tumor to check for metastases.
“We’re kind of in luck.” This was Ouyang Kan’s subconscious reaction, and he did not bother to hide it.

One of the reasons doctors from the General Surgery Department did not like to perform radical gastrectomy for stomach cancer using a laparoscope was because of limitations when it came to the parts of the abdominal cavity that could be operated on.
Radical gastrectomy for stomach cancer using a laparoscope was basically only possible for patients who were at the early stages of stomach cancer.
Even though there were research papers that delved into using this surgical method for patients who were at the advanced stages of stomach cancer, many things were still up in the air.
In short, this surgical method was only suitable for those who were in the early stages of stomach cancer.
Aside from this, stomach cancer was rarely detected at its early stages.
And even if a patient was diagnosed with early-stage stomach cancer, after laparoscopy began and a pneumoperitoneum was produced, metastases might be discovered.
In that case, what should a surgeon do?
The surgeon would have to halt the laparoscopy and carry out open surgery instead.
Since a pneumoperitoneum had been produced and an incision to insert the laparoscope had been made, there was a higher chance that more metastases would appear.
These maneuvers were risk factors for metastases to begin with.
Ouyang Kan said that they were in luck because the patient was still in the early stages of stomach cancer.
However, this was still a beginning.
Ordinarily, this surgery took five to six hours, and there were plenty of obstacles that they would have to weather.
Ouyang Kan shifted his gaze from the screen to Ling Ran’s face.
Ling Ran was wearing an earnest expression, and Ouyang Kan felt secondhand embarrassment for him.
‘Only a young person can do this.
A person of my age would never take such a huge risk and carry out such a dangerous surgery in front of so many people.’
Heated discussions were also going on in the visitation room above the operating theater.
The department director of the General Surgery Department could not help but say to Huo Congjun as he chuckled, “Young people are really impulsive.
Why didn’t you help him out and ask him to tone things down a little?”
“Why would I do that?
As emergency physicians, we never expect anything to go as we want them to.
If this world were perfect, there wouldn’t be a need for the Emergency Department,” Huo Congjun said philosophically with his hands crossed in front of his chest.
It only took one look for the department director of the General Surgery Department to know what he was thinking about.
“Are you this confident in Ling Ran?”
“With his skills, of course, I’m super confident in him.” Huo Congjun laughed.
The director of the General Surgery Department was not convinced.
“This is just the beginning.
Even if we were to disregard other things, how long do you reckon that he will take to examine the patient’s taenia coli before he can be certain that there are no metastases in there?
And what’s the probability that he won’t even be able to detect the presence of metastases?”
“The patient’s taenia coli looks thick and fair.
It seems pretty healthy.” Huo Congjun smiled.
“This doesn’t mean that there’s no metastases.”
“If a pig were to have such a taenia coli, it would probably be quite tasty.”
“Of course.
Pork intestines are delicious, to begin with.
As long as it is washed thoroughly, the taenia coli is one of the most delicious body parts of a pig.”
“There’s no point in washing it too thoroughly.”
“Forget about it.
I don’t want to be the one lying on the operating table.”

chapters.title: Chapter 819: That Won’t Happen
paragraphs: The Operating Theater 1 of the Emergency Medical Center had been renovated, was spacious, and well-designed. Even though there were a total of eight people inside, and some of them were walking around, the place was not crowded.
Even though the visitation room was similarly spacious, because of the number of people inside, the air was a little stuffy.

The experienced Associate Chief Physician Wei Qing had the intention to chase out a few resident doctors or medical interns. However, even though he had moved his lips a little, he swallowed his words in the end.

Even though surgeons were brutes, they still cared about their reputation. Aside from this, it was the politically correct thing to do to provide young doctors with a good learning environment. Senior doctors could not just chase young doctors away because they could not understand what was going on. Even though they could not understand the maneuvers in the surgery, they had their own ways of learning. No one could master a certain skill just by looking at it once. Everyone needed time to get used to things.
Besides, if he were to really chase people out, the women who were leaning against the window and taking photographs nonstop should be the ones who were chased away.

Wei Qing had been in Yun Hua Hospital for almost thirty years, but he could not really remember whether they were from the Finance Department or Public Relations Department. They might even be pharmaceutical sales representatives from third party companies.
Out of sight, out of mind. Like most of the doctors, Wei Qing fixed his gaze on the screen.

Compared with open abdominal surgery, one advantage of laparoscopy was that as long as the transmission of the signal from the operating theater was good, people who were watching the surgery got to enjoy the surgeons’ surgical field. The yellow peritoneum, spleen, stomach, and left lobe of the liver were exactly the same on the screen of the operating theater and in the screen of the visitation room. The greater omentum and transverse mesentery took up most of the surgical field...
Wei Qing suddenly regained his senses. “He’s working on the omentum already?’

“He dealt with the groups of lymph nodes in the right gastroepiploic artery and the middle colic artery at one go.” The director of the General Surgery Department looked solemnly at the operating theater below him.

Like Ouyang Kan, he had never performed radical gastrectomy for gastric surgery using a laparoscope before. It was not because he was incapable of learning it, though. It was just that gastrectomy was not exactly a high-end surgery, and as the department director, he was mainly focused on the pancreas as well as the duodenum. For general surgeons who specialized in digging patients’ sh*t, these were considered the pinnacle among surgeries.

Even though he did not know how to perform radical gastrectomy for gastric surgery, he had watched countless surgeries before. He was way more experienced compared to Ouyang Kan, and he was also a lot better at spotting various details. He only had to look at the operative route Ling Ran chose to know that Ling Ran was extremely confident.
Whenever surgeons were confident, they would take huge risks so that they could reap greater returns.
The department director of the General Surgery Department could not help but glance at Huo Congjun and say, “The patient is a policeman?”
“Yes. His parents also died while making great contributions to the country. And now he’s suffering from stomach cancer. He’s unlucky indeed,” Huo Congjun answered.
“You know, he would actually be in safer hands if the General Surgery Department were to take him in.” The department director of the General Surgery Department gave a deliberate reminder.
“Since Ling Ran is confident that he can handle this case well, let’s see how he does.”
“I’m just worried that he’s being too confident.”
“Huh?”
“Ouyang Kan from our department doesn’t know how to perform radical gastrectomy for stomach cancer using a laparoscope, so Ling Ran would have to call the shots throughout the surgery.”
Huo Congjun merely smiled and said nothing. He understood what the other party was trying to imply. As this surgery was an extremely risky one, they did not want to be responsible for it.
Of course, Huo Congjun could slap his chest and give his word that he would be responsible for everything that might happen like those dauntless sect leaders depicted in Wuxia novels.
However, Huo Congjun was not a lowly leader of a group of hooligans.
Everyone in the visitation room was quiet. Huo Congjun did not utter a word, and like a financial expert, he was determined not to hold any responsibility.
The department director of the General Surgery Department pursed his lips in disdain. “Old Huo, aren’t you being a little too irresponsible?”

“How could I be considered responsible if I were to put my subordinate in trouble?” Huo Congjun was not perturbed at all, and he looked at the other party like he was looking at a child. He then verbally attacked the other party. “You’re still young. In the future, you’ll realize what truly matters in life.”
In an instant, the department director of the General Surgery Department felt extremely angry. He was not this furious to begin with...
“Ouyang, safety first, yeah?” The director of the General Surgery Department pressed the intercom button and expressed his current emotions using a microphone.
In the operating theater downstairs, Ouyang Kan paused for a moment. However, this did not affect the progress of the surgery at all.

Surgeries like laparoscopy was a one-man show, to begin with. Even though assistants were necessary, they were nothing but props. And they would be nothing but props throughout the duration of the surgery.

Ling Ran did not even pay any heed to what other people were saying as he operated on the patient. He traced the patient’s colic artery to the superior mesenteric artery. He then found the superior mesenteric vein that was to the right of the superior mesenteric artery. Next, he exposed the right gastroepiploic vein and the colic vein. He then ligated and severed the right gastroepiploic vein at the position of its root.
After he performed this series of maneuvers, everyone inside and outside the operating theater went silent again.

Just take a couple of instructors who were standing at a basketball court and discussing the knee movements of a few students as they performed a three-step layup as an example. How would they react if one of the students suddenly performed a slam dunk?
Whether they were from the Emergency Department or the General Surgery Department, at this moment, all the doctors in the visitation room were speechless.

Ling Ran was extremely quick as he ligated and severed the blood vessel. Unlike doctors from the General Surgery Department, he was not diffident at all. After all, as a surgeon, he was used to carrying out hepatectomy. It was very normal for him to look down upon the blood vessels in the stomach. Even if the blood vessels were to burst, he was confident that he would be able to stop the bleeding.
However, what truly astonished the crowd was how familiar Ling Ran was with the anatomical structures in the abdomen.

It was relatively easy to recognize the colic artery. This was why it served as a landmark. However, after the surgeon managed to find the colic artery, it was not easy to find the superior mesenteric artery. Finding the superior mesenteric vein and the rest of the blood vessels was an even more difficult feat. If the surgeon was carrying out an open abdominal surgery, it would be relatively easy to trace the blood vessels one by one to search for relevant anatomical structures. However, it was not exactly a walk in the park. Surgeons nowadays strived to make small incisions on the patients’ abdomens, and it was hard to find certain anatomical structures by tracing the blood vessels due to the amount of tissues that served as obstacles. Surgeons might easily make a mistake.

This step was even harder when it was used during a laparoscopy. A person just had to imagine the way a young doctor had to spend one or two hours feeling around the abdominal cavity just to look for the patient’s appendix. It would be understandable if they failed to find the patient’s appendix. For surgery such as an appendectomy, a surgeon had to find more than seven or eight relevant anatomical structures.

A butcher would be able to slice a chunk of meat off the stomach in three minutes. So, why did surgeons need five or six hours to complete an appendectomy? This was because they might encounter all kinds of problems during the process. This was when the surgeon’s anatomical knowledge came into play.

When it came to surgery, as long as a surgeon was well-versed in human anatomy, was able to perform small maneuvers such as making knots and suturing well, and was good in crisis control, all that was left to be done was to merely understand the surgical method. And compared to equipping oneself with other basic knowledge, this was way too easy. It was to the point that a surgeon could manage a surgical method after only reading about it from a book.
“Spin the laparoscope downwards.” After severing the right gastroepiploic artery, Ling Ran examined the surgical field before asking Ouyang Kan who was holding the laparoscope to move it downwards.

Ouyang Kan had been mentally prepared to play the role of being called by Ling Ran to handle the surgery if anything went wrong. He was ready just in case they had to make changes and perform open abdominal surgery instead. Right then, he had totally submitted himself to Ling Ran. He slowly spun the laparoscope and exposed the bile duct, liver, stomach, and the greater omentum, which had been turned over. All of those organs could be seen on the screen.
“I’ll be using the pancreas as the landmark,” Ling Ran said so that his assistants knew what was going on.
Aside from the doctors in the operating theater, the doctors in the visitation room nodded without realizing it too.

Ouyang Kan relaxed. He could not help but glance at the patient’s face and say, “At least we’re not disappointing his deceased parents. They sacrificed their lives while protecting our country, and our country is now well-developed, with enough resources to save their son’s life.”
Ling Ran glanced at Ouyang Kan.

“We can’t just let those two people who have shed their blood at the battlefield to protect our country shed tears in heaven, don’t you think so?” Ouyang Kan could not help but feel good when he saw that the surgery was going smoothly.
Ling Ran nodded slightly. “That won’t happen.”

chapters.title: Chapter 820: Worry
paragraphs: After the surgery went on for an hour, the people in the visitation room who were not medical staff members started to look a little bored.

For people who were not in the field of medicine, stomachs and intestines were only attractive when they were soaked in red and oily hot pot soup. Meanwhile, they find those structures quite disgusting when they were soaked in crimson blood.

If a person were to disregard the big screen, the happenings in the operating theater were also starting to get a little boring. The three surgeons who were clad in blue scrubs spent most of their time looking at the big screen in the operating theater, and their hand movements were so minute that they looked like they were operating on a cricket. If people who did not know better were to watch the surgery, they would think that surgeons were even more physically inactive compared to teenage boys who spend all their time playing video games.

The sight of the two anesthetists made the onlookers even more sleepy. Compared to the attending physician, Su Jiafu at least used the computer every now and then. He would key in some stuff before deleting what he typed. He looked like a white-collar worker who was doing data entry. Meanwhile, the attending physician from the Department of Anesthesiology looked like a retard. If a person were to describe it using milder terms, he could say that the attending physician looked like he was practicing Wudang Sect’s Turtle Breathing.
The nurses, though, were busy walking around. However, the people in the visitation room were not focusing on them.

“Sigh, why don’t we just leave? The surgeons keep repeating the same maneuvers again and again throughout the surgery. Aren’t you guys tired already?” The moment a woman who was wearing a large white coat said this, the people around her realized that she was merely posing as a doctor.
“You’re right. It’s so tiring to lean against the window like this.”
“We’ve already gotten all the photographs we need, anyway. I don’t think we’ll be able to get anything new.”
“You know what? You’re right.”
“Why aren’t you leaving, then?”
“After you...”
“Are you lying to us so that you can have the whole place to yourself?”
The visitation room suddenly became lively, and the doctors there were not prepared for this.
The doctors looked at each other before they realized that the department directors and chief physicians were judging them. They immediately put the phones in their pockets.
Huo Congjun cleared his throat and said, “They’re starting to remove the level VII lymph nodes.”

“Yes, this is probably the most difficult part of the entire surgery.” Wei Qing the associate chief physician from the General Surgery Department realized that the atmosphere was awkward, and he immediately spoke up.
Huo Congjun hummed in acknowledgment. “After this, they’ll need to remove the level VIII, level IX, and level XII lymph nodes too. Those are pretty difficult to remove too, aren’t they?”

“Yes, the removal of those groups of lymph nodes is crucial too. The direction of flow and position of the arteria hepatica propria, common bile duct, as well as the hepatic portal vein, are the most important anatomical features when it comes to lymphadenectomy.” After Wei Qing spoke, he suddenly felt embarrassed. It did not feel quite right to talk about hepatic arteries, the common bile duct, and the hepatic portal vein when Ling Ran was present.

Of course, doctors from the General Surgery Department actually performed liver surgeries too. In hospitals that did not have a Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery, cholecystectomy and even hepatectomy were performed by doctors from the General Surgery Department. Professor Feng Zhixiang from Beijing believed in having a very general General Surgery Department. He was firm in his decision not to divide his department into smaller departments. In the end, he managed to establish a Center of General Surgery, and it was easy for him to delegate roles to his subordinates.

The General Surgery Department of Yun Hua Hospital was also a powerful Department. The Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery of Yun Hua Hospital was having such a hard time not only because He Yuanzheng was weak, but also because of how capable the General Surgery Department was.

On a structural level, He Yuanzheng who had transferred from another hospital was bullied by quite a number of departments. That had been going on from the day he became the department director of the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery to the present. Unless he was able to improve his capabilities or find a powerful person to back him up, in the near future, he would continue to get bullied. Fortunately, he was pretty young. If he were able to endure the humiliation and hold on to his position, after the department director of the General Surgery Department, Huo Conjun from the Emergency Department, the hospital director who used to be a surgeon, and the associate hospital directors who used to be surgeons retired, he would... be bullied by Ling Ran alone.

Now that Wei Qing was talking about the liver, the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery, as well as He Yuanzheng, came into his mind. This reminded him of Ling Ran too, and right now, he did not know what else to say.

Ling Ran’s achievements when it came to hepatobiliary and pancreatic surgery were plain to see. Aside from the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery of Yun Hua Hospital, he was also bullying the Departments of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery and even the General Surgery Departments of all the hospitals in Changxi province. He even managed to find an excellent surgeon in Beijing, Feng Zhixiang to back him up. This was mainly courtesy of his skills. Because of this, other doctors had to submit to him. But this was precisely the reason why other doctors were indignant.

Other doctors had to submit to him because a surgeon’s skills spoke for himself. As Ling Ran was one of the top hepatobiliary and pancreatic surgeons in the country, other surgeons had no choice but to submit to him. However, many chief physicians and associate chief physicians had gotten a taste of power and wanted more of it. Hence, they could not accept the fact that they were beneath Ling Ran in terms of skills and were always coming out with ways to defeat him.

“Ling Ran is pretty good at laparoscopy,” the director of the General Surgery Department said. He then changed the topic. “When it comes to radical gastrectomy for stomach cancer using a laparoscope, Southwest Hospital had actually performed quite a number of cases. From what I remember, they had already performed one thousand cases quite a few years ago. They only used this surgical method for patients who are in the early stages of stomach cancer. Based on the numbers, they should be pretty experienced at it.”
Huo Congjun arched an eyebrow when he heard that. “Is that so?”

“The doctors there wrote a research paper about it.” The department director of the General Surgery Department smiled. “If my memory isn’t failing me, they take an average of two hundred minutes to complete each surgery.”

Huo Congjun did the math and realized that they took an average of three and a half hours to complete each radical gastrectomy for stomach cancer using a laparoscope. He immediately became less adamant.

He was part of the preoperative consultation, and he knew that the surgeons planned to carry out today’s surgery for a duration of three hundred minutes. Even though there would be some discrepancies during the actual surgery, they would not be able to go a lot faster than planned.

“Speed doesn’t guarantee quality.” Even so, Huo Congjun refused to admit defeat. He looked at the operating theater and said, “When Ling Ran is fast, he can perform a hepatectomy in under an hour. However, he never strived to be fast.”
“Those doctors in Southwest Hospital didn’t strive to be fast either. It just happened naturally.”

“You’re Old Xu’s captain? Do you have your identification card with you?” As the other party looked burly, Huo Congjun did not immediately start scolding him.

Huo Congju and the department director of the General Surgery Department looked at each other. Huo Congjun sighed and said, “You go ahead.”

The department director of the General Surgery Department nodded. “The surgeons are performing lymphadenectomy now. This is mainly to prevent a recurrence. By clearing the lymph nodes around the tumor, chances of recurrence will be lower.”

Captain Chu listened earnestly as the department director of the General Surgery Department spoke. He was not in the field of medicine, and it was impossible for him to be as optimistic as a doctor. Hence, his heart was filled with nothing but worry.

chapters.title: Chapter 821: Captain Chu
paragraphs: “How’s the situation now?” Captain Chu displayed what little remained of his lovely personality when he was a child. He tried to act cute by squeezing his eyes together, as though he was trying to get rid of the goop in his eyes.

Department Director Huo sighed. “Captain Chu, didn’t we come to an agreement just now? It’s already against the rules for you to stay here and watch the surgery. If you still want to talk, it will not be suitable to the situation.”
“Just one last sentence.” Captain Chu was so anxious that his eyes almost became red.

“That’s why I said that other than being angry and anxious, the patients’ family members will serve no other purpose when they watch a doctor’s surgery?” Huo Congjun angrily scolded Captain Chu before he said, “Now, we’re watching the left edge of the hepatoduodenal ligament, and soon, we will cut the hepatogastric ligament.”
“What happens after you cut it?”

Huo Congjun said in resignation, “After we cut it, we can look for the common hepatic artery. Anyway, now, we are at the stage where we sever the connection between the stomach and liver, understand?”
“No...” Captain Chu was not in a good mood. “If I understood, why would I ask you?”
“Anyway, now we have to cut the connection between the stomach and liver. Then, we can remove the stomach.”
“Didn’t you say that you would cut only a portion of his stomach?” Captain Chu became worked up.
Huo Congjun shook his head. “We’re just removing a portion of the stomach.”
“But you just said that the surgeon will be removing the stomach.”
“It’s just a slip of the tongue.”
Captain Chu looked at Huo Congjun skeptically before he said, “If you want to remove the whole stomach, let’s stop with the surgery.”
“What? Why?” The surgeon by the side could not bear to listen to the conversation anymore.
Huo Congjun waved his hand and stopped the surgeon from speaking. He said, “Catch the main point. He has no right to decide how much of the stomach we cut and whether we want to remove it or not.”
Once he finished his words, Huo Congjun turned his head around. He did not want to bother himself with this blockhead.

Captain Chu could not accept the answer and said, “What do you mean, I can’t? I’m his immediate superior, so why can’t I decide the matter? Before Old Xu went in, he asked me to take a look for him. Don’t you doctors know how torturous total gastrectomy is? You can’t perform it, no way...”
“If no surgery means death, what would you choose?” The anesthetist by the side was angry.

Huo Congjun waved his hand again. “Please catch the main point, okay? It has nothing to do with him whether we want to perform the surgery and how much of the stomach we remove. Captain Chu, do you have the full power of attorney?”
Captain Chu was stunned a little. Then, he shook his head and said, “I don’t need that thing. I can decide.”
“Got it.” Huo Congjun confirmed his status as a blockhead again, and he was too lazy to make any further explanations.
Captain Chu had no choice but to be quiet.

A few minutes later, Captain Chu opened his mouth again. This time, he spoke slowly, “Um... Old doctor, excuse me. I was a little short-tempered earlier. Just do whatever you should do. I just want a good outcome, but I just did not know how to make it a good outcome.”
As he spoke, he also sighed heavily, and he moved to the chair behind him as if he glided there.
The young doctor who was originally sitting on the chair could only give up his seat.

Huo Congjun had been scolding people for a long time, so he also knew how to balance his words between scolding and comforting someone. Regardless of whether he was sincere or not when he admitted to his mistake, it was already not easy for him to say this in front of so many people. Huo Congjun then lowered his voice and said, “It’s just like what you said, it’s useless to blow your temper over these things. And from our perspective, there’s no need to hurry. The surgery is going smoothly, so you don’t need to be anxious, right?”
Captain Chu silently nodded.
“Do you know what surgery Doctor Ling performs most nowadays?” Huo Congjun explained from another perspective.
Captain Chu shook his head.

“Hepatectomy, and it’s several times more difficult than this surgery.” Huo Congjun did not care if there were still a few doctors from the General Surgery Department in front of him. Perhaps it was precisely because there were other doctors from the General Surgery Department that Huo Congjun had all the more reason to say this. “Look, the most difficult part for the surgery today is to cut off the part connecting the stomach and the liver before performing lymphadenectomy. But do you know how Ling Ran usually performs hepatectomy? He needs to cut off the connection between the liver and most of the other organs. Therefore, it’s not a mistake to say that the most complex organ in the abdominal cavity is the liver, yes?”
When he said the last phrase, Huo Congjun thought that it would still be for the best to provoke the director of the General Surgery Department.

Their relationship was actually good after all these years of working together. After all, they usually worked together to beat up other people. However, when they argued against each other, they would not be courteous to each other at all.
The director of the General Surgery Department was also used to it, so he replied just as rudely, “Don’t miss the pancreas.”
Huo Congjun then chuckled.
Captain Chu looked at them, and he did not want to ask any further questions.
The operating theater at the lower floor was still quiet and operated in an orderly manner.
Compared to the doctors in the visitation room at the upper floor, the doctors in the operating theater were even more focused and behaved more cordially.

For Ouyang Kan, the stomach cancer specialist, if he had been a little arrogant in the beginning because of his experience serving as his protective cover to make sure that he could provide cover for Ling Ran during the stomach cancer surgery, after being tortured for more than an hour, that protective cover had already been torn apart.
This was especially so when they approached the liver, Ouyang Kan’s arrogance was completely extinguished, and he stood aloof to all worldly desires now.

Regardless of whether the doctors of the General Surgery Department wanted to admit or not, once any surgery in the abdominal cavity involved the liver, the difficulty level would be increased by leaps and bounds. If stomach cancer surgery under laparoscopes was not good to work with because of the rich blood supply in the stomach, then liver cancer surgeries were even harder, because their blood supply was even greater.
For average doctors, if they did not undergo professional training, then when they encountered the liver, the first thing that came up to their minds would be to avoid it as much as possible.
However, how could abdominal surgeries avoid the liver?

When Ouyang Kan performed stomach cancer surgery, even if it was open abdominal surgery, he would pay extra attention to the liver. He even had some experiences unique to himself when it came to avoiding the liver, and he would earnestly execute those methods to avoid the liver.
However, Ouyang Kan did not see Ling Ran avoiding or carefully handling the liver in his maneuvers.
Ling Ran just performed according to the standard operating procedure. He solved whatever problem that appeared and handled the entire operation with brute strength.
Ouyang Kan wanted to say something at the beginning, but after he hesitated for a few minutes, he did not have the intention to talk anymore.

Ling Ran, who had performed thousands of liver surgeries, possessed his own effective strategy in handling the liver, and in this strategy, whatever that Ouyang Kan thought that was stupid might be the better or safer choice Ling Ran discovered after polished his skills repeatedly.

Naturally, it could possibly be a stupid choice, but considering Ling Ran’s great records and experience, as well as Ling Ran’s familiarity towards the liver, Ouyang Kan dared not recklessly point out what he thought was foolish.
“Do you want to have someone else take your place so that you can rest?” Ling Ran suddenly asked.

Ouyang Kan was stunned. He suddenly realized that he did not hold the laparoscope well. But as the person in charge of his treatment group, he had not held a laparoscope for someone else for a long time.
“No need, I’m alright. Apologies for the mistake.” Ouyang Kan kept apologizing as if he had suddenly returned to the past when he was a junior doctor.
“Okay,” Ling Ran answered, then he said calmly, “The surgery time is longer, so you can just tell me if you want to take a rest. In between, you can also have a meal.”
“Alright,” Ouyang Kan quickly answered.
“We’ll continue if you don’t want to have someone take your place.”
“No need, let’s continue.”
“Let’s eat steamboat tonight.” Ling Ran took some time to make this decision before he happily continued the surgery.
Captain Chu at the upper floor did not know what expression he should show now.

chapters.title: Chapter 822: Break
paragraphs: “Doctor Ling.”
“Doctor.”
“Huh?”
“Yeah...”

When doctors walked out of the door that led to the corridor in the operating area, the patients’ families in the waiting area came forward and surrounded them. Old Xu’s wife and son were moved to the front like an unwanted parcel being passed around.

“The surgery is successful. You can watch from outside the ICU after the patient wakes up.” Ling Ran gave a simple statement and showed a smile befitting societal norms to comfort the patient’s family.

From Ling Ran’s observation, most doctors would not smile in this situation. Having a stern expression while talking to the patients was the norm. Ling Ran agreed to this strategy, but based on his personal experience, a general, polite, and pure smile could also make people feel at ease.
The people in the waiting area outside the operating area needed to feel at ease the most.
Old Xu’s wife and son did indeed feel a little relieved, but they did not know whether it was because of the completion of the surgery or whether it was because of Ling Ran’s smile.

“The patient is rather young, so his body condition is better. Now, if he is sent to the ICU, he can get better nursing care, and his recovery will be relatively better. Mister Xu’s insurance provides quite the complete coverage, so most of his ICU fees can be claimed...” Zuo Cidian slowly spoke while he stood beside Ling Ran and tried hard to draw the possible wrath from the patient’s family to himself.

“Just send him to the ICU. We’ll follow Doctor Ling’s instruction.” Old Xu’s superior, Captain Chu, who had average looks, was quite the crude person, was suspected to be the kind to cause medical disputes, and had a lot of annoying things he needed to deal with, came out from another side, and he made the decision for Old Xu’s wife.
Old Xu’s wife was originally at a loss. When she saw Captain Chu making a decision for her, she just nodded and agreed to it.
Zuo Cidian sighed in relief. After dealing with many doctor-patient relationships, he was also afraid of encountering weird people.

“Um... Doctor Ling, let me give you a treat tonight. After all, performing surgeries is a hard task.” Captain Chu chuckled. He had annoyed Huo Congjun and the others to their limit, but he also collected sufficient information, which allowed him to verify that the doctors in the operating theater were really good, and their performance was great as well.
Once he came to this conclusion from his indirect “interrogation”, Captain Chu was naturally in a good mood, and he was also willing to spend a bit of his income to give a treat.
Ling Ran naturally shook his head. “No need.”

“You don’t have to be bothered by all the trivialities. I have already booked the place. Restaurant Great Red Country, and we’ll get the best room there. Everyone must go,” Captain Chu shouted at the top of his voice.
Zuo Cidian must stand forward to talk when they encountered this kind of situation. With a troubled look, he said, “Captain Chu, we’re not going. Doctor Ling also doesn’t like to go out for meals.”
“Go, everyone must go.” Huo Congjun came from the back.
Captain Chu showed a happy face. “Department Director Huo, you’re smart...”
“I have invited the leader of your city bureau, so I’ll talk to him properly later.” Huo Congjun snorted. “Two tables. I’ll treat your leader on one, while you treat our Ling Ran on the other one.”
Huo Congjun said fearlessly in front of everyone, “As a police officer, you pretended to be a doctor to enter the hospital’s operating area. That’s not allowed. ”
Captain Chu was stunned.

“Doctor Ling, I’ll blanch some tripes for you. You just need to blanch black tripes for eight seconds, and they’ll be ready to be served. They’ll be perfectly crunchy by then. If it’s cooked, it may not be so delicious.” Captain Chu passionately acted as a waiter. All of his future obedience was overdrawn, and he even loaned some of that attitude from payday loan companies.
Ling Ran stared at Captain Chu using the public chopsticks and spoon, thanked him, and said, “I can blanch them myself, you don’t have to do it for me.”

“I’m really grateful to you. Old Xu’s family doesn’t have someone who can take charge right now, so I can only help out a little. Sigh, it must not be easy for you. You’ve saved his life, after all.” As Captain Chu spoke, he put another tripe into Ling Ran’s bowl again.

The tripe which was blanched for only eight seconds was really fresh and crunchy. After Ling Ran ate it, he nodded slightly and said, “You’re welcome. In truth, other doctors can also perform stomach cancer surgery.”
Master Level Gastrectomy was not something that required Ling Ran to be proud of as of current. If he were to be ranked on the national scale right now, he might only be among the top one hundred.
When he thought about this, Ling Ran quietly asked the system, ‘System, what is the rank for my gastrectomy skill?’

“The gastrectomy skill that you mastered is ranked first in Yun Hua City, first in Changxi Province, and 48th in China. If you perform another two hundred to three hundred gastrectomies with no mistakes, you might be promoted by one further rank,” the system answered very clearly.

Ling Ran was slightly surprised. Being ranked 48th in the country did not actually mean there were forty-eight incredibly good gastrectomy specialists in the country, because they may be like him who mastered M-Tang technique, Achilles tendon repair technique, hepatectomy, and other skills. The more skilled the doctor was, the more skills he might have possibly mastered. Just like the experts in the General Surgery Department, it was impossible for them to fail in intestinal surgery when they could perform stomach surgeries well. Doctors who could perform hepatectomies well might be good in gastrectomy as well.
This was why Ling Ran felt that his ranking should be slightly lower.
However, when he considered how his other skills might have added to his skill level in gastrectomy, he could also understand why he was ranked at that position.

Captain Chu continued counting the time he needed to blanch the tripe, chuckled, and said, “I don’t know about other doctors, but Doctor Ling, you performed the surgery for Old Xu, so we feel very thankful. It must not have been easy to save Old Xu’s life.”

“After the surgery, he still needs to continue with chemotherapy. We don’t know what his subsequent treatment plans are yet.” Ling Ran reminded him. In China, the recurrence rate in three years for early-stage stomach cancer was generally lower than 10%, but its recurrence rate in five years would be increased to 15% to 20%, and this was not considered low. Besides, a single patient would only reach this statistic when they received all sorts of treatment methods.
If cancer recurred, the patient’s survival rate would be very low, and there were very few people who could live over three years.

Captain Chu remained silent for a few seconds before he smiled in a manner as if a burden had been removed from his shoulders. “Let’s just see how it’ll go. I am not his father, so I’ll just do as much as I can.”

“Captain Chu, I counted with my watch just now. You’re really accurate when it comes to the eight-second count. It’s exactly eight seconds.” Lu Wenbin was still a young man. He did not like to listen to this kind of topic that already had its conclusion set in stone. He was more interested in tripes.

Captain Chu smiled. “When we are on a mission, we often need to calculate the time. When the superior says to release the dogs in eight seconds, but you released them in seven seconds, you’ll be scolded when you go back.”
Lu Wenbin came to a realization, and he was slightly regretful. “So, this is still dependent on experience, and practice makes perfect?”
“Naturally.”
“What a pity.”

Captain Chu laughed. “If you want to practice, I can arrange some practice sessions for you. We have a training site. But those in our field get injured easily. Look at my knee. I fell from a wall one year during my service, and I never recovered from it. I can’t even run properly now.”
“Haven’t you seen a doctor for it?”
“I have. How could I not have? But the doctor said that I need to undergo surgery, and I was afraid, so I’ve been delaying treatment.”
“What diagnosis did he or she come up with?”
“Something like injury on the meniscus?”

Lu Wenbin could not help but laugh. “You should look for Doctor Ling for meniscus injuries. The knee arthroscopic meniscoplasty Doctor Ling performs is so good that there are patients coming from other countries for treatment.”
Captain Chu was stunned for eight seconds before he stood up, placed two tripes into the skimmer spoon and said, “Doctor Ling, I’ll place my knee into your hands. Let me blanch some tripes for you.”

chapters.title: Chapter 823: Is It Still Possible?
paragraphs: One week later, the people and dogs in Yun Hua Police Dog Unit—mostly the people—gathered together and surrounded a hospital bed.
The team members said some auspicious words sincerely.
“Captain, you need to be healthy.”
“Captain, don’t be afraid when you enter. It will be over in the blink of an eye.”
“Captain, don’t be afraid. Yuan Wang and I will wait for you outside the operating theater.”
Captain Chu opened his eyes in a second, like Cao Cao waking up from his sleep. His sight was as sharp as a sword. It was as if he wanted to kill someone. “Yuan Wang died a long time ago.”

“I brought along Yuan Wang’s photo so that it’ll bless you.” That team member carried a deceased dog’s portrait while he smiled at the captain. The deceased dog in the portrait was a German Shepherd, but it was so ugly that it looked like a mix between a German Shepherd and a Labrador Retriever; its smile was even photoshopped on it by the team member.
Captain Chu was angry but also felt resigned. “Old Yang, I told you that I applied for a new police dog for you, right? Don’t carry around Yuan Wang’s portrait everywhere.”
“You said that last year, and I still haven’t seen my pup yet.”
“I think you’re the pup. Is there anyone out there who would carry a deceased dog’s portrait to visit their captain?”
“Keep your voice down, or else, Yuan Wang will be unhappy if it hears you.” Old Yang pretended to cover the dog’s ears on the portrait.
Captain Chu was so mad that he laughed. “If I’m not on an IV right now, I will smack your head, do you believe me?”

“You didn’t even smack me when your knees were still good, so what should I be afraid of?” Old Yang held the deceased dog’s portrait and swung it in front of Captain Chu. “If you don’t give me a dog, I will whack my head and spill my blood all over your body.”

“Old Yang, stop it. You’ve been causing a whole ruckus all for one dog.” The vice-captain who stood at the front could not bear with him anymore and said, “Be more serious. The captain is going for surgery. Since everyone is here... Attention, salute!”
The group of people who surrounded the hospital bed saluted Captain Chu, who laid on the bed. The atmosphere was very solemn.
Eight seconds later, laughing sounds were heard in the ward, and even Old Xu, who had only recently gotten out of his bed, kept patting the wheelchair while he grimaced in pain.
Lu Wenbin also laughed when he listened to the stories. Then, he could not help but said, “All of you are really naughty.”

“It’s good to be slightly naughty. The dog who survives for the longest time is always the naughtiest one. The old, hardworking dog will usually get hurt and be forced to retire, even if it doesn’t die while on duty.” Captain Chu took a look at his knee as he spoke. His knee was not injured once or twice only. At the end of the day, it was all the fault of enduring hardships and working hard.
“Alright, family members, please leave.” Lu Wenbin waved his hand and started to chase people away.
The group of people also did not say anything else. They left the room.
It was only when they were about to leave that they said some actual good words.
“Captain Chu, you have to be good during the surgery later.”
“It’s just a minor surgery, don’t be afraid. Learn from Old Xu.”

“Captain, look at the foreigners, they are all here for Doctor Ling for their surgeries, so you don’t have to worry about entering the operating theater. If he’s not good, they wouldn’t dare recommend him to foreigners. ”
Old Xu also showed a faint smile on his face and said to Lu Wenbin, whom he was familiar with, “Doctor Lu, we’ll pass Captain Chu to your team now.”

“Alright. You can just find a place to rest first. Knee arthroscopic meniscoplasties are surgeries that will end very quickly. At most, it will take you the time to eat two pork trotters.” As Lu Wenbin spoke, he pointed at the waiting room. There was a pot of pork trotters. There was no brand and no shop name for it, but it released an aroma that people could hardly reject.
That group of people subconsciously walked over, as if they had a spell on them, and they were fixed on the spot around the pot.
Lu Wenbin quickly rushed to the operating theater.

Knee arthroscopic meniscoplasties were his favorite type of surgery. Compared with M-Tang technique surgeries, the difficulty of entry-level knee arthroscopy was much lower. Naturally, when knee arthroscopy was developed to a higher level, the difficulty level would not be low. However, most doctors did not need to master such high-ended skills to perform knee arthroscopy. This was very attractive for young doctors, especially young doctors who rarely had a chance to perform surgery.
M-Tang technique required two to three years of learning and another three to four years for the doctor to be skilled with the skill, so it was not something all doctors could bear.

Lu Wenbin could be the chief surgeon for the M-Tang technique now because of Ling Ran giving him guidance and chances. But even so, Lu Wenbin only dared to handle the simple medical cases. When he encountered the more difficult cases, he could only give them away, and the feeling he experienced at that time could only be depression.
Knee arthroscopy was more user-friendly. Theoretically, it only took a few months for a person to improve his skills in knee arthroscopy to the point that he could become a chief surgeon.
Some doctors from people’s hospitals and county hospitals just went for internships in the big hospitals for one to two months, and after that, they were able to leave to perform such a surgery.
Ling Ran’s demands were slightly higher, but the doctors he trained had much better skill.
When a doctor was at Lu Wenbin’s age, once he decided to continue his career as a doctor, the attraction of skills to him can be said to be fatal.
Captain Chu was pushed into Operating Theater 1 soon.
Normal doctors would not use Operating Theater 1 that contained a visitation room.

The wide and bright visitation room was a dream place for experts to pretend to be awesome, but it was not comfortable for normal doctors. Besides, the visitation room made it so that the visitations in Operating Theater 1 were different from the visitations in other operating theaters. The chief surgeons could usually use excuses like those visiting doctors disturbed the progress of the surgery or disturbed the surgeons’ mood and chase out the visiting guests whom they did not like. However, the visitation room was a totally independent space from the operating theater. The chief surgeon did not have the right to chase people away, and he also needed to bear judgment from everyone. If he were not skilled at a certain level, he would not be able to stand it even if he was shameless.
Ling Ran was naturally a regular guest in Operating Theater 1.
He liked Operating Theater 1 not only because Operating Theater 1 was wide and bright, but also its hygienic level was very high from Ling Ran’s perspective.

Operating theaters were not always clean. An absolutely clean operating theater did not exist, or else, all those nosocomial infections would not have happened. In hospitals with a high turnover rate, most operating theaters kept a certain level of cleanliness. If anyone wanted them to put more effort and time into improving the cleanliness of the operating theatres by 100% or 200%, there must be someone with unique power supervising them.
Examples of those with unique power would be the high ranking leaders who will always appear in the visitation room at some point in time.
The people’s gazes and scrutiny were not in Ling Ran’s range of consideration.

“Doctor Ling, I’ll have to rely on you now.” Captain Chu chose regional anesthesia for his knee arthroscopy, and he showed great obedience on his face as if he was facing a loan shark who came to collect his final payment.
Ling Ran raised his hands and stood in front of Captain Chu while waiting for the anesthesia to take effect. He also nodded slightly.

He wore a blue scrub, had a stern expression, and was surrounded by a variety of instruments for knee arthroscopy. There were also a few busy doctors working in the operating theater, and all these things made Captain Chu’s face quickly become stiff.
“We should renovate the interrogation room like the hospital. The difficulty of interrogation would be greatly reduced.” Captain Chu still tried to be talkative to reduce his diffidence.
Yu Yuan passed by him and asked, “Aren’t you in charge of raising dogs only?”

“Are you joking?” Captain Chu became angry. “The major cases handled by us, the Police Dog Unit, are top of the crop. Don’t look down on our police dogs. The drug dealers and killers are all scared when they see our police dogs—”
“What if your dogs fight for food?” Yu Yuan asked again.
Captain Chu was stunned. “Do you raise a dog?”
“Just curious.” Yu Yuan smiled faintly.
*Shick.*

The airtight access door of the operating theater was stepped open, and Lu Wenbin entered after he washed his hands. He looked at Yu Yuan with a guarded expression and said, “Doctor Yu, I am the assistant for this surgery.”
“I know, I’m just helping you to make the patient relieved.” Yu Yuan smiled at Captain Chu before she glanced at Lu Wenbin and was ready to leave.
Captain Chu’s lips twitched, and his eyes were full of doubt.
At this time, Ling Ran said, “Since you’re here, just observe the surgery. It’s rare.”
Yu Yuan was stunned a little, then she asked, “Rare? How rare is it?”

“The internal part of the patient’s knee is completely smashed, so it’s quite rare.” Ling Ran raised his chin and said, “There was a previous case who had his knee in a worse condition than this patient’s, and it should be that patient who practices mixed martial arts. ”
“I remember him. That person’s knees were almost broken into pieces.” There was nothing wrong with Yu Yuan’s memory.
Ling Ran nodded. “Right.”
Lu Wenbin also spoke, “That fellow ate two pork trotters at once. Germans are so good at eating.”

Captain Chu stared at the three doctors and listened to their conversation. Then, he suddenly felt regretful and asked the anesthetist in a low voice, “Is it still possible for me to choose general anesthesia?”

In hospitals with a high turnover rate, most operating theaters kept a certain level of cleanliness.
If anyone wanted them to put more effort and time into improving the cleanliness of the operating theatres by 100% or 200%, there must be someone with unique power supervising them.
Examples of those with unique power would be the high ranking leaders who will always appear in the visitation room at some point in time.
The people’s gazes and scrutiny were not in Ling Ran’s range of consideration.

“Doctor Ling, I’ll have to rely on you now.” Captain Chu chose regional anesthesia for his knee arthroscopy, and he showed great obedience on his face as if he was facing a loan shark who came to collect his final payment.
Ling Ran raised his hands and stood in front of Captain Chu while waiting for the anesthesia to take effect.
He also nodded slightly.
He wore a blue scrub, had a stern expression, and was surrounded by a variety of instruments for knee arthroscopy.
There were also a few busy doctors working in the operating theater, and all these things made Captain Chu’s face quickly become stiff.
“We should renovate the interrogation room like the hospital.
The difficulty of interrogation would be greatly reduced.” Captain Chu still tried to be talkative to reduce his diffidence.
Yu Yuan passed by him and asked, “Aren’t you in charge of raising dogs only?”
“Are you joking?” Captain Chu became angry.
“The major cases handled by us, the Police Dog Unit, are top of the crop.
Don’t look down on our police dogs.
The drug dealers and killers are all scared when they see our police dogs—”
“What if your dogs fight for food?” Yu Yuan asked again.
Captain Chu was stunned.
“Do you raise a dog?”
“Just curious.” Yu Yuan smiled faintly.
*Shick.*
The airtight access door of the operating theater was stepped open, and Lu Wenbin entered after he washed his hands.
He looked at Yu Yuan with a guarded expression and said, “Doctor Yu, I am the assistant for this surgery.”
“I know, I’m just helping you to make the patient relieved.” Yu Yuan smiled at Captain Chu before she glanced at Lu Wenbin and was ready to leave.
Captain Chu’s lips twitched, and his eyes were full of doubt.
At this time, Ling Ran said, “Since you’re here, just observe the surgery.
It’s rare.”
Yu Yuan was stunned a little, then she asked, “Rare?
How rare is it?”

“The internal part of the patient’s knee is completely smashed, so it’s quite rare.” Ling Ran raised his chin and said, “There was a previous case who had his knee in a worse condition than this patient’s, and it should be that patient who practices mixed martial arts. ”
“I remember him.
That person’s knees were almost broken into pieces.” There was nothing wrong with Yu Yuan’s memory.
Ling Ran nodded.
“Right.”
Lu Wenbin also spoke, “That fellow ate two pork trotters at once.
Germans are so good at eating.”
Captain Chu stared at the three doctors and listened to their conversation.
Then, he suddenly felt regretful and asked the anesthetist in a low voice, “Is it still possible for me to choose general anesthesia?”

chapters.title: Chapter 824: Serious
paragraphs: “The meniscus has a longitudinal tear and a posterior horn tear. The situation is worse than we thought.”
“There’s also an anterior cruciate ligament injury acting as an associate injury, and it’s rather serious.
“The old injuries are also quite serious.”
Ling Ran asked Lu Wenbin to show the MRI scans on the screen before he explained to Lu Wenbin and Yu Yuan.

This operation was by all means, a minor operation. There were altogether six consecutive knee arthroscopy operations scheduled on that day, and it was not possible to perform complete preoperative preparations for them, like hepatectomy. It was also not necessary because even if the medical staff made preparations and explained things in advance, it would be impossible for the surgeons to remember, and it was even more dangerous for them to misremember.

The surgical plans for knee arthroscopy surgeries for non-athletes were basically the same, because the internal structure of the knee joint was simple enough. Hence, it was easy to tell whether the surgery could be done or not. Of course, some were performed well and some were performed badly, but it was not easy to completely screw it up.
Of course, as the patient, Captain Chu did not have such an easy time.

Captain Chu, who chose to have regional anesthesia, was sitting on a cold operating table with his legs down and a green drape over and above his knees. If he were a pretty and young girl sitting by the riverside, this scene would probably still be beautiful.
However, as he was an old policeman with a weathered face, it was nowhere close to that effect.
“My knee is usually fine.” Captain Chu listened to them talk about all kinds of “serious” situations in his knee, and he felt as guilty as a smuggler being sniffed out by dogs.

Lu Wenbin said with a serious expression, “Your knee is like a house. The knees of normal people are like normal houses, where the steel frames and cement are all positioned neatly and tidily. When the meniscus of the knee joint is damaged, it’s just like a collapsed ceiling. Your knee joint... is like something built from rubble. If it were a house, it’ll still be liveable, but as for the living conditions... You know it yourself.”

Suddenly, Captain Chu was full of bitterness, yet he remained in optimistic denial. He tried to be funny. “Aren’t you describing it really seriously, though? Is it because you want to charge me more for the surgery? I’m telling you, I’m a police officer, and it’s illegal to charge more for surgeries... ”
The three doctors looked at Captain Chu without smiling.
“Let him sleep a while.” Ling Ran felt that Captain Chu was talking a little too much.

“Sleeping sounds good.” Captain Chu also felt that the atmosphere was too uncomfortable. He watched the anesthetist injected a tube of medicine into him, and while he was still conscious, he quickly said, “Doctor Ling, our police team has a lot of teammates with bad knee joints, if you cure me, I will send them all here. I won’t take any commissions... ”
Lu Wenbin took a peek at Ling Ran and bent over to whisper to Yu Yuan, “He knows the rules, alright.”

Captain Chu opened his eyes, yawned, stretched his hands to reach out for his phone above his head. After fumbling for it three times and not managing to feel it, he felt somewhat anxious, and he sat up so fiercely that his bed rattled.
“You just finished a surgery, remember?” Su Jiafu came over on a round stool, like he was Dumbledore on a broom.
Captain Chu rubbed his head and realized what was going on after looking at Su Jiafu. “Right, I just had surgery.”

“Yeah, the operation was very successful. I’ll give you a test.” Su Jiafu stood across Captain Chu lackadaisically. As an anesthetist who often did anesthesia for hepatectomy patients, Su Jiafu was now very confident. To say it plainly, Doctor Su Jiafu was currently at the phase where he was feeling full of himself, and he regarded performing anesthesia such as anesthesia for knee arthroscopy with a disdain, but only a little.
After performing the check-up step by step, Su Jiafu nodded again and said to Captain Chu, “You can stay for another hour before going back. At present, the recovery progress looks very good.”
“I don’t have to go back to the ward?”
“We’ll be sending all of you together over there in a while.” Su Jiafu gestured with his chin and motioned to both sides.
Captain Chu looked at both sides, before he noticed that there were people lying on the beds next to him.

The recovery room in the Operating Area was not like a ward that had rooms with triple beds and quadruple beds. The recovery room was just a room, and there was a gap of only around three feet between each bed. When things got busy, there would even be ten beds in the room. Anyway, since they were watched by an anesthetist or up to two anesthetists, as long as nothing happened, things were alright.

The state of mind of the newly awakened patients was not something to look forward to. Fortunately, all the characters who had just undergone surgery will and can basically lie on the bed obediently. The anesthetists’ task in the recovery room was to watch them wake up normally, and then transfer them out of the room.
Captain Chu rested for a few minutes with his eyes closed before he opened his eyes again. Out of professional habit, he asked the people beside him, “What surgery did you undergo?”
“Knee arthroscopy.” The patient on the bed next to him was about forty to fifty years old. He was rubbing his head as if he had a headache.
“Did you also go under general anesthesia?” Captain Chu rubbed his head as well.
“Yeap.”
“Why did you take general anesthesia for knee arthroscopy?” Captain Chu asked curiously.

When he reached this topic, the patient next to him said in slight displeasure, “It’s said that there was an idiot who took his surgery before us. He seems to be a policeman or something, and he was damn talkative, which affected the doctors’ surgery. After that, all patients were required to undergo general anesthesia.”
Captain Chu subconsciously hunched his shoulders.
“I guess general anaesthesia’s fine since you won’t feel anything. What about you?” The person beside him seemed to be in the mood to talk now.
“Almost the same, I guess. I fell asleep too.”
While talking, another patient was sent in and placed on the other side of Captain Chu.
“Knee arthroscopy as well?” Captain Chu was somewhat getting familiar with the tell-tale signs.
The nurse anaesthetist connected the ECG monitor to the patient and said, “Doctor Ling is mainly doing knee arthroscopy today, and there may be more being sent over.”
“He performed so many in one go?”

“It’s the normal amount for him.” The anesthetist did not explain further. Nowadays, with Ling Ran’s rising fame, more and more patients looked for Doctor Ling for surgery. If he accumulated patients requiring knee arthroscopy for half a month to a month, he will be able to operate on them for a full day.
However, Ling Ran would not really perform knee arthroscopy surgeries for an entire day.

To his current self, knee arthroscopy was almost elementary. It was a bit like having a professional athlete kick a penalty kick to an undefended goal. Although missing the kick was definitely possible, under normal circumstances, the probability of making mistakes was too low.
Once the challenge in knee arthroscopy was gone, for Ling Ran, there was no appeal in staying up late for surgery.

It was also mainly because knee arthroscopies only had a narrow skill branch. If there was no other temptation in front of the skill branch, then there will be a lack of motivation for the people at the back to continue climbing up that branch until the top.
Ling Ran operated on patients until dinner time, and that was the end of his surgeries for the day. He handed over his work and went home.
In the parking lot, a Rolls Royce was parked next to Ling Ran’s small Volkswagen Jetta.
When she saw Ling Ran arriving, the door to the Rolls-Royce opened, and a young girl ran out and went to the bus across the Rolls-Royce and slapped at the door madly.
A few seconds later, Tian Qi came down from the bus and explained with slight embarrassment, “The space in the RV is a little bit bigger...
“By the way, why did you get off work so early today, Ling Ran?”
“I was done with today’s arthroscopies.” Ling Ran shrugged.
“Let’s go have some barbeque, then. Your cattle should already be fattened.” Tian Qi opened her eyes wide and stared at Ling Ran.
“Okay, let’s go get barbeque.” Ling Ran nodded and agreed.

chapters.title: Chapter 825: Tranquility in Companionship
paragraphs: After driving ten minutes from the highway in the rural area of Yun Hua City, a lake and a hill could be seen.

There were cows on the hill. Some were strolling about while some went to the lake and drank. Some went straight ahead to rest under the shadow of the trees. They were so relaxed that they looked like the leaders in some state-owned enterprises.
Even when the workers sat in pickup trucks drove over fiercely, the cows looked at them lazily and did not even bother to move away.

“Lift them up!” The foreman in the pickup truck urged everyone to immediately set up the logs that were placed at the back of the truck to set up a bonfire. Then, they set up tents to block the wind and, within 15 minutes, a whole campsite was set up.
The foreman looked at the cows with malicious intent. He started to recite the poem with his hands behind his back, “Who dares to oppose me when I want to cross the road?”
The Zebus from Brazil either looked at him at a loss, in contempt, ignored him, or were just too stupid to move. But none of them moved.
“Foreman Li, I saw it very clearly. That foremost cow is ridiculously fat.” The workers cooperated with the foreman and pointed out the cow to be sacrificed today.

“Okay. Those who block the trucks will be removed. This message has been given to all the cows before. Go, give it a swift end!” The foreman posed handsomely and let the wind in the farm blow through his shirt, making it flutter loudly.
The workers swarmed up and pulled away the fat cow that seemed lost.
Soon after, a big black bus stopped at the campsite that was newly set up.
The foreman immediately ran over and waited in front of the big bus with his back bent.
Tian Qi and Ling Ran came down after one another.

Ling Ran looked around curiously. He always had a sense of curiosity and thus, he was the most serious and meticulous student during the dissection sessions during class. So, Ling Ran had many questions to ask about this hidden farm cum meadow that was near Yun Hua.

“Why is there a meadow here?” Ling Ran was born and brought up at Yun Hua. When he saw this stretch of grass covered land, he could not help but feel some emotions stir in his heart, just like when a man who lived in the desert saw a big manmade lake.

The meadow in front of him had real grass growing on it. If he did not turn around and look at the highway, he will have the misconception that he was staring at grass over an endless stretch of land with wind blowing through it, and when he lowered his head, all he saw will be cows and sheep.

Tian Qi thought carefully and said, “For the meadow... In the beginning, I had a piece of land, so we planted some vegetables to supply greens to our family. Later, I think we used it to rear chickens, ducks, geese, pigs, and other animals. Then, someone in the family opened a restaurant and did not have a place to keep purchased cows, I think? I don’t quite remember...”
The foreman looked at Ling Ran tentatively. He then saw the obscenely handsome young man nodded and agreed to what Tian Qi said.

The foreman immediately lowered his head in case others saw his expression. Miss Tian’s reason was so bad that it was not even worth deliberating to know that it was fake. Was it really okay to think that it was the truth?
But to Ling Ran, some excuses did not need any sort of pondering to be accepted.

Take, for example, the fruit stall in front of Yun Hua University, when he went and bought fruits, he could always get the fragrant and sweet fruits, but when his coursemates went and bought them, the fruits differed in quality. Was there any reason worth pondering over why this was the case? Of course, there was not.
Ling Ran nodded and saw the workers carrying a big cow over.
“Is this the Zebu brought over from Brazil?” Ling Ran looked at the cow’s body, which was just pure flesh.

“Yes. I thought of grilling the whole cow, but Chef Zhu said that while grilling the whole cow is only for aesthetic purposes, it won’t taste good.” Tian Qi looked at Ling Ran’s expression, smiled, and said, “If you want to eat a whole roasted cow, we can make an appointment and have one done another day.”
“Let’s try today’s cow first.” Ling Ran looked at the meadow, which was something he rarely saw, then looked at the sky slowly becoming dark, and he felt a great sense of comfort in his heart.

Tian Qi felt happy when she saw that Ling Ran was happy. She gestured for someone to come over and take over all the details of getting the cow ready. Then, she sat down with Ling Ran and said, “Do you want to grill the beef on your own, or do you want the chef to do it for you?”
“Let the chef do it.” Ling Ran smiled. “I already grilled a lot of stuff today.”
The barbeque taste made from the endotherm knife was not comparable to grilled beef.

A chef who looked rather familiar personally used the knife and removed a tenderloin from the cow which had already been processed and was hanging by the side before he cut it into big pieces, skewered them, and grilled them on the spot. He then whispered in a low voice, “Chef Zhu is making the beef entrails inside, but I often cut up the cow and roast the beef as well.”
“Thank you.” Ling Ran did not care about it either way, and he did not say much either.
The view in the sky was not bad, and the heat from the bonfire was warm. It was the exact temperature that made him feel most comfortable.
Tian Qi also relaxed.

It was only when she saw two skewers of beef being served in front of her that she snapped out of her daze and smiled. She took one of them and passed Ling Ran the other. She asked, “Are you still busy lately? Did you perform a lot of surgeries?”
“Yes.”
“You perform more surgeries than other doctors, right? What’s the feeling of performing so many surgeries?”

“I feel good most of the time. I performed a stomach cancer surgery a few days ago... Hmm... If humans have four stomachs, the surgery will be simpler,” Ling Ran said while looking at the cow at the side.
Tian Qi thought about it and said, “But cows can’t go having one stomach missing either, right? Therefore, the probability of getting liver cancer should be four times higher for them, isn’t it?”

“It is not quite accurate to calculate it this way either” Ling Ran thought about it and said slowly, “It should be around one time to four times higher, but we’ll have to analyze the entire situation again if we want to think about the specifics.”
“Make sense.” Tian Qi agreed on it.
Ling Ran touched his chin and thought for a moment. Then he ate the beef skewer and asked, “What have you been up to recently?”

“My grandfather asked me to take over a few companies to practice my skills.” Tian Qi pursed her lips, “Compared to your life, that’s much more boring. All of them are companies that are not entirely necessary in the market. The only reason to buy them is just to get rid of potential competitors and increase the occupancy rate of our company. This kind of thing will happen every few years. It’s really boring. But doctors don’t have to worry about their competitors, right?”

Ling Ran thought about it and nodded slowly. “Doctors will always have multiple paths available for them to take when it comes to their development, just like Department Director He from the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery. He is now focusing on liver cancer and bile duct cancer.”

Tian Qi certainly knew about He Yuanzheng. She covered her mouth and smiled. “It might also be because companies aren’t humans. That’s why companies will always greedily try to take in all resources available, but doctors are human. There will come a time for them to retire and eventually die.”
Ling Ran nodded. “The golden period of a doctor’s life is truly short.”
“That won’t happen to you, Doctor Ling.” Tian Qi smiled faintly and passed one newly grilled beef to Ling Ran.
The blazing bonfire illuminated the grass around them and caused the beef to release a fragrance of the meadow, which can never be found in the beef served from restaurants in the city.
The quiet starry sky seemed to look at the ground, giving off a sense of alienation, but it also brought forth a precious tranquility to the place.
